title: Label Cleanup Heuristic Cookbook (personal draft)
content:
Quick personal reference for common cleanup / reconciliation moves we keep repeating during QA. This is a messy scratchpad — capture recurring rules, quick examples, and heuristics to turn into a short-team playbook later.

Goals:
- Reduce inter-annotator drift for weird tokens and concatenations.
- Make consistent choices for noisy user text (IDs, run-together words, mixed-language fragments).
- Provide quick fallback rules when label is ambiguous.

Principles (high-level):
1) Prefer deterministic, low-effort rules that are easy to check automatically (regex-first) and add manual review only for low-confidence/complex cases.
2) Keep "do no harm": when in doubt, prefer a conservative label (e.g., label as OTHER / UNK rather than assigning an incorrect entity).
3) Document the exception pattern + one example so reviewers can confirm.

Heuristics / rules (ordered by frequency):
- Long numeric/string IDs with separators (dash/underscore/period): treat as single token unless clearly human-readable (e.g., invoice12345 vs invoice-123-45).
  - Rule: If token length > 8 and contains both letters and numbers, and separators are only [-_.], label as ID/SYS (system-id) instead of splitting.
  - Example: "user_000123abc" -> ID/SYS (don't split). Rationale: these are system artifacts and splitting produces noise.

- Email-ish tokens and handles: if token matches user@domain pattern, label as CONTACT if the task requires PII identification; otherwise mark as TEXT_SAFE and redact in downstream datasets.
  - Edge: slack-like handles (@team-bot) - treat as MENTION, separate from email.

- Concatenated words (camelCase, snake_case, kebab-case):
  - camelCase: try a light split to identify readable words only when both sides yield dictionary words with length >= 3. If not, keep as ONE token.
    - Example: "orderHistory" -> split into order + History -> label ORDER, ACTION if context requires. But "getUsrId" -> keep as ONE token and mark as CODE/UNK.
  - snake_case / kebab-case: split on _ and - unless tokens are <3 or look like IDs.

- Mixed-script tokens (Latin + CJK or Cyrillic):
  - Heuristic: treat switch of script within token as boundary -> split into two tokens and label independently.
  - Note: occasional transliteration merged into Latin (e.g., "zhongguoChina") — prefer split.

- Currency amounts with attached symbols ("$100USD", "100€EUR"): normalize to [CURRENCY][AMOUNT] two tokens in the labeled data; keep original raw in metadata.

- Nested entities (person name inside org string, e.g., "Google - Sundar Pichai"): prioritization rule: if both appear, label both with separate spans and store relation tag ORG:has_leader. If labeling schema doesn't support relations, prefer ORG span over PERSON unless labeling task is person-centric.

- Hyphenated compounds:
  - If both sides are dictionary words and the compound is meaningful (e.g., "state-of-the-art"), label as single ADJ or CONCEPT span.
  - If one side is short/abbrev or numeric ("COVID-19", "GCP-us-west1"), preserve as single token with subtype (DISEASE/REGION).

Confidence thresholds / QA routing suggestions:
- Apply automated rules with high-confidence labels. If rule returns confidence < 0.75, route to quick-review queue.
- Quick-review queue batching: group similar ambiguous messages (same regex pattern) and review 20 at a time — much faster than single examples.

Label actions cheat-sheet (action -> when to use -> quick regex):
- KEEP (no change) -> clear and high-confidence token (names, clear dates) -> N/A
- SPLIT -> concatenated readable words or mixed-script boundaries -> camelCase / _ / - with /[A-Z][a-z]+/ etc
- MERGE -> when tokenization split produced parts of a named-entity ("San" "Francisco") incorrectly separated by tokenization bug -> rejoin if both tokens are consecutive and match known gazetteer
- MASK -> PII that we must not store (SSN-like) -> /\b\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}\b/
- RECLASS -> initial automatic label guessed wrong; reassign to top-priority schema label during cleanup

Quick examples (raw -> suggested labeled span + rationale):
- "invoice: INV_2023112-AQ78" -> INV_2023112-AQ78 (ID/SYS); keep as single span. Rationale: internal invoice id.
- "reach me at priya.shah+test@gmail.com" -> "priya.shah+test@gmail.com" (PII/EMAIL) -> MASK for exported dataset.
- "GCP-us-west1-pool-03" -> single span REGION/RESOURCE. Rationale: infra resource name.
- "SalePrice$199.99incltax" -> split into SalePrice (FIELD) + $199.99 (AMOUNT) + incltax (FLAG). Rationale: units and semantic meaning differ.
- "100percent" -> split into 100 + percent (NUMBER + UNIT) if downstream task uses numeric normalization. Otherwise keep as TEXT.

Open questions / follow-ups to formalize into team playbook:
- How do we represent multi-span relations elegantly in our current labeling UI? (file ticket for UI support)
- Do we want a consolidated regex set that runs pre-labeling and auto-tags everything that matches? (pro: speeds QA; con: hides edge differences)
- Thresholds for quick-review routing: 0.75 is arbitrary — can we mine historical disagreement rates to pick a better cutoff?

Notes-to-self (things I noticed in last QA batch):
- Many annotators split camelCase aggressively even when it yields non-words -> need explicit examples in the labeling guide.
- Tokenizer version mismatch across export pipelines causing lots of merged tokens with trailing punctuation -> raise infra PR to standardize tokenizer version in dataset exports.
- Some labelers keep hyphens, some drop them; add a "preserve hyphen" guideline per entity type.

Small action list (next steps):
- Draft a 1-page cheat-sheet for labeling UI with 10 canonical examples + preferred action. (owner: Priya)
- Add a pre-labeling regex pass to the labeling pipeline to tag obvious IDs/PIIs (owner: Marco).
- Run disagreement analysis on last 5k labeled items to determine automatic routing threshold (owner: Lena).

If I forget this: the core idea is "automate safe cases, surface ambiguous ones in batches, document the one-rule exceptions".

-- end of scratchpad --

(Still messy; plan to prune and convert to a shared doc once we confirm regex list.)
